access: browser (news lists load by script); article pages also via WebFetch

entries.title: Origin pages: Honduras, Brazil, Colombia (read 18 Nov 2026)
key_points: Honduras: harvest November–April; IHCAFE regions Copán, Opalaca, Montecillos, Comayagua, El Paraíso, Agalta; almost all farms above 1,000 m; ~95% smallholders.
Brazil: Sul de Minas, Mogiana and Matas de Minas pick April–September, Cerrado May–September; Santos 17/18 and Rio Minas 17/18 named as main types.
Colombia: fresh coffee most of the year, with the mitaca about six months after the main crop; southern departments (Huila, Cauca, Nariño, south Tolima) are the largest by volume.
No offer lists with differentials were shown publicly on the origin pages.

entries.title: Vietnam 2026/2027 Harvest Update
key_points: Robusta seen above 32m bags (+3%) and arabica above 1.5m bags (+15%).
Northern arabica picking runs mid-September to December; Lam Dong from late November into early February.
Drier, El Niño-type weather is helping harvest pace and quality; higher fertiliser prices lift growers' costs.

entries.title: Central America and Mexico 2026/27 Harvest Update
key_points: Region seen below 18m bags (−9.3%) after a 19.68m-bag 2025/26 crop; off-year arabica plus a hot, dry Q3.
Honduras and Mexico fall most, then Guatemala; bean-filling problems at low altitudes in western Honduras.
Early picking from October, peak December–February; quality is the main uncertainty (more stock lots, fewer exportable grades).

entries.title: Kenya – Tanzania Harvest Update
key_points: Kenya's 2026/27 main crop is expected larger, led by Kiambu and Kirinyaga, with consistent quality; Tanzania also up.

entries.title: Colombia 2026/27 Main Crop Update
key_points: Heavy rain at February–March flowering, then dryness in June–July: main crop expected no bigger than the already small 2025/26 crop.
Main-crop flow from October, heaviest through December.

entries.title: Tanzania 2026 Harvest Update
key_points: Crop seen 4–5% larger as new plantings come in; arabica ~40% picked, robusta 80–90%.

entries.title: Indonesia & Timor-Leste 2026 Harvest Update
key_points: Indonesia 20–40% smaller after excess rain at flowering; ripening is longer and uneven, which makes crop sizing harder.
Robusta ~80% picked with over 60% already sold; Sumatra arabica runs into Q1 2027.

entries.title: Brazil 2026/27 Late Harvest Update
key_points: Crop kept at 75.4m bags with arabica +27%; robusta about 4% lower.
Harvest slow after May–June rains: 45.2% done on 26 June vs 52.1% a year earlier and a 51% average; arabica picking into September.
Bean size good: about 25% of arabica on screen 17+, about 70% of robusta on screen 13+.

entries.title: Peru Harvest Update 2026
key_points: Volume about 7% lower (off-year plus rain >20% above normal at flowering); fewer low grades and borer, good quality.

entries.title: East Africa Mid-Year Harvest Update 2026
key_points: Rwanda about 35% smaller (poor flowering, less fertiliser subsidy).
Uganda's main robusta harvest 4–6 weeks late, tightening nearby supply; volume broadly stable.

entries.title: Colombia 2026 Harvest Update (mitaca)
key_points: Mitaca from mid-April, lower altitudes peak late May–June, higher zones June–July, done by mid-September.
Volume about 4.5% below last year's mitaca; good quality and low borer; heavy Q1 rain a risk for main-crop flowering.

entries.title: Indonesia Harvest Update 2026
key_points: Second straight year of lower output on excess rain; quality held by careful processing.

entries.title: Uganda's Arabica Crop Outlook
key_points: National arabica output about 100,000 bags lower on late and poor rains.

entries.title: Brazil 2026/27 Harvest Update
key_points: Record 75.4m bags (+15.5%): arabica 49.4m (+26%), robusta 26m (flat).
Robusta picked March–July, arabica April–October by region; uniform ripening and larger beans expected.

entries.title: Burundi and Rwanda Harvest Update 2026
key_points: Burundi up over 60% to about 24,000 t, harvest a month early (from ~10 March); Rwanda about 16,000 t.

entries.title: Central America Crop Progression Update 2025/26
key_points: 2025/26 region crop near 18m bags (+4.5%) on better plant health after record 2024/25 revenues; harvest ends late March–April.
